nodes.description: ACAD9 functions as a mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I assembly factor, binding the assembly factors NDUFAF1 and ECSIT within the MCIA complex. Biallelic ACAD9 variants impair this assembly-factor role. Although ACAD9 belongs to the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family and retains residual long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity, its disease-relevant essential function is complex I assembly, not fatty acid oxidation flux.

nodes.description: High-dose riboflavin (vitamin B2), the precursor of the FAD cofactor, improves complex I activity in the majority of patient-derived fibroblasts and in many treated patients, and is associated with significantly better survival in early-onset disease. The proposed mechanism is that increased mitochondrial FAD supports FAD binding and improves ACAD9 folding and stability, thereby promoting complex I assembly.
